summary.description: DeepCAC2 is a two-stage deep learning pipeline for coronary artery calcification assessment in chest CT. It first uses an nnU-Net-based cardiac segmentation model to localize the heart, then applies a patch-based 3D U-Net to segment coronary artery calcifications and derive Agatston calcium scores and risk categories.

inputs.label: Chest CT
inputs.description: Non-contrast, low-dose chest CT scan in DICOM format.

outputs.label: Predicted Agatston Score
outputs.description: Automated coronary artery calcium score derived from the predicted CAC segmentation.

model.architecture: Two-stage pipeline with nnU-Net-based cardiac segmentation followed by patch-based 3D U-Net CAC segmentation.

details.name: DeepCAC2
details.devteam: Artificial Intelligence in Medicine Program, Mass General Brigham / Harvard Medical School
details.cite: Nürnberg L, Bernatz S, Foldyna B, Lu MT, Fedorov A, Aerts HJWL. Coronary artery calcification assessment in National Lung Screening Trial CT images (DeepCAC2).

publications.title: Coronary artery calcification assessment in National Lung Screening Trial CT images (DeepCAC2)

use.title: Intended use
use.text: DeepCAC2 is designed for automated coronary artery calcification (CAC) segmentation and cardiovascular risk assessment from non-contrast chest CT scans, enabling opportunistic screening without dedicated cardiac CT protocols. The generated outputs and dataset can be explored via an interactive public dashboard [1] and are derived from the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) cohort available through the Imaging Data Commons (IDC) [2].

analyses.title: Analyses
analyses.text: The pipeline produces volumetric segmentations of the heart and coronary artery calcifications, from which Agatston calcium scores (CACS) are computed and mapped to categorical risk groups (0, 1–100, 101–300, >300). These standardized outputs enable cohort stratification, longitudinal analyses, survival modeling, and reproducible imaging biomarker research at scale [1].

evaluation.title: Evaluation
evaluation.text: DeepCAC2 was evaluated for both technical validity and clinical relevance. Technical validation compared automated CAC scores and risk categories against expert annotations on a subset of NLST scans, demonstrating high agreement. Clinical validation using survival analysis showed that model-derived CAC risk groups are strong independent predictors of all-cause mortality, with clear stratification across risk categories [1].

entries.Adjusted covariates: Age, sex, smoking status, heart disease

training.title: Training
training.text: The CAC segmentation model was trained in a supervised manner using 778 ECG-gated chest CT scans from the Framingham Heart Study with expert CAC annotations. The pipeline uses a two-stage approach: nnU-Net-based cardiac segmentation followed by patch-based 3D U-Net training on balanced overlapping 3D patches extracted from heart-centered volumes [1].

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.text: The model is optimized for non-contrast, low-dose chest CT scans and may be sensitive to variations in acquisition protocols, reconstruction parameters, and image quality. CAC quantification is derived from non-ECG-gated scans, which may introduce motion-related inaccuracies compared to dedicated cardiac CT. Generalization to other populations, scanners, and clinical workflows requires further validation [1].
